transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ava Johnson (ZenCare CTO), Samir Patel (ZenCare ML Lead), Maya Li (ZenCare SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): Redwood model catalog walkthrough, demo of API + Console + Optimize. Discussion of open models (Llama-2 variants, Mistral, other open weights), tradeoffs between hosted/dedicated/private, quantization and integer types, and benchmark numbers.

Topics: Model selection, performance profiles, compatibility matrix, deployment modes, next steps for POC.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Sofia from Redwood, i'll be running the demo with Marco the SE. quick intro round?
[00:10] Ava: Hey i'm Ava CTO at ZenCare, we own platform and infra decisions.
[00:16] Samir: Samir ML Lead, i'll be primary on model selection and evals.
[00:21] Maya: Maya SRE, i'm here for security and infra questions.
[00:25] Marco: Great, thanks. we'll start in the model catalog in the Console then flip to the API and show Optimize recommendations.
[00:35] Sofia: Quick note, this recording's for internal use, we'll share the deck, model catalog PDF and a compatibility matrix after.
[00:45] Marco: Pulling up the Console, top-level is the model catalog. you can filter by capability (chat, completion, embeddings), size, license and verified perf. for example we have a verified profile for Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, and a bunch of quantized variants.
[01:05] Ava: When you say verified profile, what does that include? latency numbers? cost?
[01:10] Marco: Yeah we run standardized benchmarks across hardware families, sequence lengths, and common prompt sets. profile includes median p50/p95 latency, throughput in tokens per second, and token cost estimates assuming our hosted price or dedicated unit cost. also notes on compatibility: like whether int8 or int4 quant passes for that model on a given GPU.
[01:30] Samir: Do you have a matrix for VM types and specific kernels? we run on A100s and some T4s in edge spots.
[01:38] Marco: Yup, the compatibility matrix maps model variant -> GPU family -> recommended quantization and kernel. for example Llama-2-13B fp16 shows best on A100 with cuBLAS+custom kernels, int8 works on A100 and T4 but with a perf delta and sometimes slightly higher latency p95.
[01:55] Maya: question on private deployments, we need KMS/HSM integration and V P C endpoints — is that supported?
[02:02] Sofia: yes, for Private we support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering, audit logs, SAML SSO. we'll share the SOC two pack and our network docs.
[02:15] Ava: good. on the model side, were worried about hallucinations in our healthcare domain. how do you evaluate quality?
[02:23] Marco: We run eval suites tied to customer prompt sets and can run regression alerts in Optimize. For ZenCare we can seed the benchmark with your QA prompts to measure ROUGE/EM and factuality metrics. we'll store the evals and alert on drift.
[02:40] Samir: Cool. show me an example benchmark.
[02:45] Marco: flipping to Benchmarks tab — here's a Llama-2-13B run: p50 token latency ~12ms on A100 for 1k context with batching turned off, p95 around 48ms; throughput at 32 tokens/second with our continuous batching policies. note these numbers vary by sequence length and batching.
[03:10] Samir: 48ms p95 seems optimistic, that was for single-request on A100? what's the kernel config?
[03:18] Marco: single-stream with KV cache enabled, compiled kernel set A (our optimized attention). When using int8 quant, p50 jumps to ~9ms but p95 can widen due to kernel fallback on certain sequences, so we annotate that in the profile.
[03:35] Ava: can we compare Llama-2-13B vs Mistral-7B for cost/perf?
[03:42] Marco: Yup — side-by-side view. Mistral-7B at fp16 gives lower token cost and better throughput; Llama-2-13B has slightly higher quality on our evaluated prompts but higher token cost. Optimize will recommend model+quantization combos based on a target quality threshold you set.
[04:05] Maya: what about embeddings? we rely on dense vectors for search, do you run embedding models in the catalog too?
[04:12] Sofia: Yes, embeddings are in the catalog. you can pin an embeddings model per route, and see vector dims, latency, and cost/per-embedding.
[04:20] Samir: There's often a mismatch between cloud benchmark and our infra. can you run benchmarks with our exact prompts and tokens?
[04:26] Marco: Absolutely — we call that a customer prompt-run. we'll take your sample set, run it across candidate models and quant settings on the target hardware (we can use Dedicated or your Private infra), and return CSVs with p50/p95/throughput and quality metrics.
[04:45] Ava: security again — are logs PII redacted before leaving the private cluster to your control plane?
[04:52] Sofia: For Private deployments, logs can be configured to never leave the VPC; for Dedicated/Hosted we have retention controls and PII redaction tooling. we'll include the exact options in the security pack.
[05:05] Samir: there's a row in your compatibility matrix about KV cache persistence — what's the impact?
[05:12] Marco: KV cache helps reduce compute for multi-turn, but some quantized kernels need special KV layout; the matrix flags which kernels support streaming KV and which require recompute. we also show expected token cost savings for typical chat patterns.
[05:30] Sofia: quick demo of the API: here's a POST to /v1/generate, you can pass model: "redwood-llama-2-13b-fp16" or a catalog alias. we support streaming, function calls, and structured output parsers.
[05:50] Samir: aliasing is nice. we plan to pin model versions in prod, can Redwood handle rollouts?
[05:57] Marco: yes, Console has rollout policies: canary, percentage-based, and automatic fallback to a configured fallback variant. we log per-route performance so you can compare.
[06:10] Maya: network egress costs? if we run Dedicated in a cloud region, can you help estimate egress and compute costs?
[06:18] Sofia: we include approximate unit economics in the catalog profiles and can run a cost model for your traffic traces if you share anonymized usage.
[06:28] Ava: any known gaps - like models that are tricky to quantize?
[06:32] Marco: Certain models with custom attention patterns or alibi-style positional encoding can be trickier. we mark those in the catalog under "compatibility notes". sometimes we fallback to fp16 for stability.
[06:46] Samir: show me Optimize — how would it recommend configurations?
[06:50] Marco: Optimize ingests your workload (prompt shapes, target latency/cost constraints) and suggests batching, cache TTLs, quant profiles, and model variants. here's an example: for a 99th percentile latency target of 200ms and 10k QPS, it recommended Mistral-7B int8 + 2000-token cache + 16-request batch.
[07:15] Ava: interesting. can Optimize hook into our CI to detect regressions?
[07:20] Marco: yes, you can link an eval set and get regression alerts; we also support webhook integrations to your monitoring or Slack.
[07:30] Maya: ok logistically, for the POC we want three things: 1) a benchmark run on our prompts across 3 candidate models, 2) the compatibility matrix for our A100/T4 fleet, and 3) SOC2/security docs.
[07:41] Sofia: agreed, we'll own 1 and 2; security pack to Maya. putting due dates in follow-up.
[07:48] Samir: timeline — want to decide model by end of month, can you meet that?
[07:52] Sofia: yes if we run benchmarks this week we can have results next week and a scoping call mid next week.
[07:58] Ava: cost question — if we start hosted and later move to Dedicated, what's the migration friction?
[08:05] Marco: migration is supported; since model variants and rollout configs are consistent across modes, you mostly change routing and capacity. we'll help with data migration considerations if you store logs or embeddings.
[08:20] (small cross-talk)
[08:30] Sofia: ok last slide is recap. next steps are: send model catalog PDF + compatibility matrix, run benchmarks with Samir's prompt set, share SOC2 and SSO docs, and schedule dedicated/private scoping.
[08:45] Ava: sounds good thanks.
[08:48] Marco: thanks everyone.
[08:50] End of recording

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings ("V P C" spaced, "SOC two" instead of SOC2), punctuation roughness; speaker labels are mostly correct.

References/links shared: https://redwood.ai/model-catalog (demo link, placeholder), shared drive: /decks/zen-care-model-catalog.pdf, benchmark sheet: link to shared CSV (to be uploaded).
